one_star_reviews.text: I don’t usually like posting negative reviews, but I felt I had to share my experience. My partner and I visited the Onehunga Forever New store to purchase a pair of heels, but unfortunately, the service was very disappointing. The staff member was busy on her phone and did not greet us, offer any assistance, or provide much customer service. When we were purchasing the sandals, she asked if we would like to become Forever New members, which we were happy to do. However, the process of taking our details and receiving the confirmation was poorly handled, and unfortunately, our points were also not credited. We later visited Forever New at Sylvia Park, where the staff member was extremely friendly and helpful, which made the contrast in service even more noticeable. Overall, we had a really disappointing experience at the Onehunga store and hope the customer service can be improved.

Honestly, one of the most frustrating experiences I’ve had with a healthcare provider.

I was clearly told that 24 hours’ notice is required if I need to cancel or change an appointment, otherwise I may be charged a cancellation/late fee. Yet apparently that rule only applies to patients.

The clinic had no problem cancelling my appointment just 3 hours before it was scheduled, despite knowing that patients have to organise their lives around these appointments. I had already arranged and paid for a babysitter specifically so I could attend. My time and money were apparently not worth the same consideration they expect from their patients.

And when I tried to reschedule, the next available appointment was not until the end of the week. So I’m expected to give 24 hours’ notice and potentially pay a fee, while the clinic can cancel at the last minute and leave me waiting for days with no apparent accountability.

Things happen, and I understand that emergencies can occur. But if you’re going to enforce strict cancellation policies on patients, you should have the professionalism and courtesy to hold yourselves to the same standard.

I went to Tony’s for a puncture repair and mentioned that I’d used Tony’s before, including having a Tony’s Car Service sticker on my car. I was also 100% certain that I had previously purchased my Michelin and Bridgestone tyres from the Wairau Park branch. (He said 'we never have sold Michelin' - well google Tonys and Michelin and you will see they did).

When they checked my history, however, there was no record of either tyre purchase. I couldn’t find the original invoice, so I understand that makes it difficult for them to verify the purchases, and I accept that.

What disappointed me was the way the situation was handled. There was no attempt to offer any goodwill or discuss options, it was essentially straight to charging my credit card. I found the attitude quite stern and the overall customer service pretty poor.

I understand that not having the invoice is ultimately my issue, but given that I’ve used Tony’s before, I expected a little more consideration.

Needless to say, I won’t be going back. I’ll happily pay the $40 or so elsewhere for a puncture repair and take my business somewhere I feel a bit more appreciated.

one_star_reviews.text:
I do not recommend studying at Whitecliffe.

My experience has been deeply disappointing. I came here because I genuinely wanted to develop my skills in art and jewellery and receive a quality education, but I feel that the education and resources provided have fallen well short of what I expected for the amount of money and time students invest.

The curriculum has also changed in ways that have meant lessons and techniques I specifically wanted to learn have been cut or reduced. As an art and design student, that is incredibly frustrating when you are paying for an education that is supposed to develop your practical skills and prepare you for the industry.

There are also serious concerns about the learning environment and workshop facilities. Ventilation has been inadequate, particularly when working around fumes, and I have witnessed students and staff becoming unwell in these conditions. For the first couple of years I attended, there was also no air conditioning, which made working in the studios extremely uncomfortable.

Administration has also placed significant demands on teaching staff. Teachers have been required to attend meetings during teaching time, taking them away from their students and adding to workloads that already appear extremely heavy. I’ve seen staff become stressed and overworked, and inevitably that affects the students’ education and support.

I’ve personally experienced poor communication around assessments and extensions as well, creating unnecessary stress and uncertainty that could have been avoided with clearer administration.

Overall, I have increasingly felt that financial and administrative priorities are being placed ahead of the quality of education and the wellbeing of students and staff. I came here wanting to be encouraged, challenged and developed as an artist and jeweller. Instead, I have often felt like students and teachers are left to make do with inadequate resources and increasingly difficult circumstances.

I am disappointed by the amount of money, time and energy I have invested here. At this point, I am primarily sticking it out because I want to finish the degree. If I had known beforehand what my experience would be like, I would have seriously considered studying in Europe instead.

Students come to an art school to learn and develop their skills. The institution should be building its students and staff up, not continually putting them under additional pressure.

I frequently send international parcels in last few months and have always used the same NZ Post process: I complete all the required information on the NZ Post website, pay online, print the shipping label, and then drop the parcel off at an NZ Post branch.

For the first time, I happened to visit the Johnsonville branch because it was convenient. Unfortunately, the experience was extremely frustrating. The staff members refused to accept my parcel.

They questioned whether the address I had entered was valid, despite the fact that I had completed it according to NZ Post's own online requirements and had successfully used the same format multiple times before. Their objection seemed to be based on their own understanding rather than NZ Post's official system and requirements.

I genuinely appreciate NZ Post employing older staff members and providing opportunities for people of different ages. However, if staff are going to be responsible for accepting international parcels, they need to receive proper training on NZ Post's own online postage system, payment processes, and address requirements.

Please train your staff properly. Customers should not be turned away simply because the employees personal understanding does not match NZ Post's official procedures.

I am extremely disappointed with my experience at this centre.

I had an appointment at 11:15 am today for an IUD removal but was charged for an IUD replacement, despite not receiving that service. I attempted MULTIPLE times to change my appointment online to a removal only, but the booking system did not provide an option to do so.

When I raised this with reception, I was told I should have called to change the appointment. However, my confirmation email specifically stated that appointments could only be changed through the original booking method, which I had already attempted to do unsuccessfully.

I do not believe it is fair for patients to be financially penalised for limitations or faults with the centre’s own booking system. Being charged for a service that was not provided is particularly concerning when accessing healthcare is already a financial burden for many people.

Healthcare providers should be prioritising patient care, transparency and accessibility, rather than leaving patients feeling pressured into paying for services they did not receive. This experience has left me feeling incredibly frustrated and disappointed, and it has unfortunately damaged my trust in this centre.

I have requested a refund for the difference charged for a service I did not receive. I strongly encourage the centre to review its online booking system and refund policies to ensure other patients do not find themselves in the same situation.

Patients seeking healthcare deserve better communication, fair treatment and a booking system that actually works. Unfortunately, based on this experience, I would not feel comfortable returning.

one_star_reviews.text: I had a disappointing experience with this recruitment agency. Communication was inconsistent, and I often had to follow up multiple times to get basic updates. Despite promising timely feedback, they failed to provide any meaningful information about my application progress. The overall process felt disorganized, and I did not feel supported as a candidate. I would not rely on this agency for future opportunities.

I couldn't imagine a worse experience if I tried.

I needed documents sent to a PO box in Auckland. They also needed to include a self-addressed, pre-paid courier bag so they could be returned to me. Pretty simple.

Tried to go in at 4:40 on Monday, and despite having an open sign the doors were locked.

Went in Tuesday and again the door was locked so I had to wait for them to come back from lunch, the owner seemed absolutely baffled and passed me off to his coworker.

I was asked to email them the details, which I did. I stated several times this issue was time sensitive, and I was happy to pay extra to have things settled quickly. Was told to leave it with them, and they'd sort everything out.

Later that day I got an email asking for the same details again, which I sent through.

I emailed Wednesday (after trying to call and not getting an answer) to confirm the package had been sent, got a reply saying they needed me to again confirm my address (which they had on file and was already in the first email, plus I had given them in person).

I sent an email yesterday as I still hadn't received a tracking number, and when I didn't receive a reply I went in person. Was told they had only just sent the documents.

Today, Friday, I find they put my return address as the destination. So after an entire week of being jerked around, I paid to have my documents delivered to my own house.

To make matters worse, they didn't even include the return courier bag in the parcel.

I went down to my local paper plus and had the whole thing sorted within 15 minutes.

I'm honestly stunned. I've dealt with these guys in the past and never had a problem, so I assume they must be under new management. Absolutely can't recommend them for anything important or time sensitive.

EDIT: I posted a review over a year ago. While I knew then that SST was a horrible place, I’m only now, after being out for a couple of years, fully realising just how bad my experience there actually was.

I am genuinely so much better off having left this place, but I still struggle with the long-term impact it had on me. I already had CPTSD prior to SST and this place only traumatised me further. It pushed me to the brink of nearly not being here anymore.

They’ll act welcoming and supportive at first. They’ll tell you they care, that you’ll be safe, and that they provide a caring and supportive environment. DON’T fall for it.

This was far from a safe/supportive environment. I repeatedly had concerns ignored, including concerns relating to safety. There was also clear favouritism towards certain residents, which made an already horrific environment even worse. If you were someone who questioned things, thought for yourself, or pointed out faults with how things were being handled, you became a “problem” rather than someone whose concerns were worth listening to.

There were situations where I was told I was being aggressive when I wasn't. There is a massive difference between someone being genuinely aggressive and someone being frustrated because nobody will properly listen to them - ever.

You can beg staff to listen/help you, but they couldn’t care less. At the end of the day, they get to go home. Residents don't have that luxury. You are left living in the environment that they can walk away from at the end of their shift, and there was no consideration given to what that does to a young person.

My physical health is also a huge part of my experience. I became chronically unwell while living there, and there were countless occasions where I was belittled or dismissed when I was too unwell to function normally. To the point I had to quit my job of nearly 5 years while I was living there. I was told I just had to get on with things, even when I simply couldn’t. There were also times where I was refused prescribed medication because staff either couldn't or wouldn't administer it, whether because of inadequate training, not knowing how to give it, or just not wanting to.

I know that staff weren't my doctors (thankfully) and they couldn't act as such. However, that doesn’t excuse repeatedly dismissing someone who is clearly unwell or forcing them to do things when they are genuinely not physically capable of doing them.

I’m still sick to this day. I have since been diagnosed with serious health issues. The lack of support and the repeated pressure to push through being unwell likely contributed to how badly my health deteriorated. I'm not claiming that residential caused all of this, but I do know I was very unwell while I was there, I needed support, and I did not receive it.

To any current or former staff member reading this: what may have seemed like a minor inconvenience, exaggeration, or joke to you was (and still is) my actual life.

Despite repeatedly raising concerns, I saw no action taken. This is something I am now seriously considering taking further now that I have been out for a while and have had the time/distance to properly process everything.

One of the most significant impacts this place had on me was what it did to my ability to trust and seek help. I already struggled hugely with this, so when you live in a place where speaking up gets you dismissed, ignored, or treated as the problem, you only continue believing asking for help is not worth it.

Looking back, I wish someone had told me not to go. I wish someone told me that the bs they present to you isn't what you will actually experience once you are living there.

So to any families/potential clients considering this place: I BEG you not to. It isn’t this amazing and therapeutic place they make it out to be.

SST did not help me. It made me worse. I am doing far better without this organisation in my life. I only wish I had never had to live it in the first place.

Please, stay away - at all costs

one_star_reviews.text:
Booked an appointment in 2020 at the age of 24 to try prevent future hair loss as I had noticed shedding, and was really upset about it. I was sold over $1000 of products and got no results. Was new to the hair loss journey, and was trying to catch things to prevent needing an expensive hair transplant surgery. this place didn’t even recommend me Finasteride (which I didn’t even know existed) one of the most proven medicines for hair loss. It’s now 2026, I’ve only recently found out more from my actual qualified GP, that Finasteride even exists - and is perfect for my case. I’m lucky and don’t have any side effects from Finasteride. So try it before going here. Save yourself the money. my GP was shocked at the upsell and medical medicine avoidance by Clive Clinics - for their own expensive overpriced product sales. They capitalised on my anxiety about my hair loss and my lack of confidence and they didn’t even help me. I have since had to undergo hair transplant surgery, because for years after coming here I was too upset to deal with the problem elsewhere. I ended up having to spend thousands on a hair transplant to repair the damage, and am now on Finasteride to prevent future loss - which Clive should have origionally recommended me to go on. I wish years ago I just went to my GP instead of this group.

The effect this has had on me mentally has been extreme and has effected my daily life for far too long. I’m very sad that this group did not help me to get on Finasteride back in 2020. My goal was to prevent hair loss and catch it early, and they didn’t even tell me anything about this official proven widely used medicine, Finasteride, other than selling me their own products - that did nothing to help me other than cost me huge expense. My Finasteride costs $5 for 3 months of medicine and is very effective at preventing further hair loss. In comparison to $1000 approx every 3 months for their products I think it was. All I can rememeber was the cost was extreme, and it was like an expensive subscription I just needed to buy and buy again. They completely capitalised off my health.

Read other reviews - I’m not the only one who has had this experience.

This google account is not my full name, Clive clinics can reply to this and I will contact them if they wish to discuss this with me. I have receipts from back when I engaged their services.

Very saddened I was not given correct advice, ended up having to have surgery to repair the continual damage, and only recently found out about Finasteride by my GP.

Has they recommended me Finasteride, I would not have even needed to get a hair transplant surgery as my hair loss was extremely minor. I went to them to try catch it before it got worse - and they ripped me off and I was too saddened and demoralised to go to anyone else since, until recently when I finally took action to go to my GP, discuss my case, and start Finasteride and only recently, finally repair the damage done with surgery.

Clive also told me all different reasons why the hair loss could be. They never discussed genetics, my father / grandfathers hair and how it is genetic DHT susceptibility - aka, perfect candidate for cheap Finasteride. They ripped me off.

one_star_reviews.text:
Funeral directors and staff were very helpful and understanding at first
But unfortunately a lot of mistakes were made and it taken us 6 weeks since our mother passed to convey our concerns after the initial shock and grieving
My wife and I chose an ashes box and a small travel urn for mums ashes 4 days before the service
Upon arriving to pick them up an hour before service the staff informed us they did not have the main ashes box there and someone was trying to find one in a warehouse, they asked if they could drop her off at the service which was not ideal as we were very perticulated about transporting her ourselves.
They then offered to let us choose another urn at no extra cost, which was acceptable and nice of them.
Again they asked if they could drop her off.
Again we said no we will wait.
They then came back out with name plate for us to check which was incorrectly printed!
Again offered to drop off at service, which we gave an abrupt NO . We realised and commented where the travel urn was as we needed it to transport a small amount of ashes to mums home town of Tukannu to plant a Kōwhai tree there, they looked confused and then the receptionist found it on her desk from where we had paid for it 4 days prior. Again they asked to drop off!!!! They then brought out travel urn with ashes in and went back to sort main urn and name plate.
By this stage there was about 15 minutes before service started
My brother and I walked out to our car with travel urn in hand while we waited, then upon walking back inside saw a trail of ASHES from our car all the way in doors and even more huge mess of ashes all over their dark beautiful FOYER!!!!!!
We held up urn which had a manufacturing hole in bottom!!!!! We found celitape on desk so patch it !!! Staff then came out win main urn for service, my brother commented “ you might want to clean my mother up off your floor”!!!!!
The staff were speechless and so were we 😢😢now we had to just leave as service was 5 minutes away to start.
It was all a bit shocking and we left without discussing anything as we’re already not thinking straight as you would expect with grieving
In my experience these events and where our mother’s ashes were spilled would come with some kind of spiritual tapu or bad karma.
Oh and upon arrival to service realised ashes in travel urn were packed incorrectly and leaking around edges😳🥵
We were all a rather upset of course but don’t want to be nasty or malicious but at least would of expected a heart felt apology which have not received
But in saying that we have not followed this up
Overall not happy about any of this but managed to send our mother off with great respect in the end
Don’t hold any animosity towards simplicity funerals as I think they were as shocked as us at these events
Also a little bit funny as our mother said she wanted to be scattered everywhere, so she got her true last wishes

I came to this temple with a pure heart, deep devotion, and the hope of experiencing peace, spirituality, and the divine blessings of God. But sadly, my experience here has been extremely disappointing and heartbreaking.

It is truly upsetting to see a place that is meant to be sacred and spiritual feel more commercial than devotional. It is now 6:30 PM, and the main deities are still closed for personal puja, with devotees not being allowed to worship and have darshan as they came for. Instead, we are expected to wait, follow numerous restrictions, and even be quiet because we have come with our children.

But why do devotees come to a temple? To experience the presence of God, to pray, and to find peace , not to feel restricted, disappointed, or unwelcome.

As a genuine devotee, this experience has deeply hurt me. A temple should be a place where faith is nurtured, devotion is respected, and people feel connected to God. It should never leave devotees feeling that commercial interests are taking priority over their spiritual experience.

Honestly, I regret coming here today. I would rather choose another temple where I can pray peacefully and feel the true essence of devotion than return to a place where the spiritual experience feels overshadowed by restrictions and commercialisation.

God is the reason we come to a temple. Devotion should come before business, and faith should never be made to feel like a transaction.

I came seeking divine blessings, but I am leaving with a heavy heart. 🙏💔

My daughter loves BK, when ever travelling this is her first stop with her friends, until now… we often have to go to Nelson and Christchurch, this time we went to Nelson for a conference and the first stop was BK.  They had an injured person with them, so it took them time to get in and out of the car, then to get into the restaurant, sit down and order.  The order took about 10min, they collected, and ate their lunch. They went back for seconds, as hungry boys often do, spending about $80 all up. They left when they had finished.

A few days later my daughter gets a fine in the mail for $85 because she was 11min over Burger King’s car park.

I find this disgusting for a number of reasons.
1: it takes time to eat, most restaurants allow 90 minutes a sitting.
2: they had an injured person with them which takes time to get them out of a car, back into a car, and into the actual restaurant, then seat them and sort out food for them before getting their own.
3: boys no matter what age, like to eat, and after travelling 3 hours, then doing a workout, they will eat. To go back for seconds is not uncommon and takes time for each order to come through.

It appears to me, that this branch of Burger King does not wish to have customers that would like to sit and enjoy a meal, and go back for seconds.. my daughter and her friends have severely been put off going to this branch and won’t be returning.

There isn’t even a meter to pay for parking, you are only allowed 1hr, 1 or 2 minutes over and you will be slapped with an $85 fine, a risk this lot are not prepared to take again.

one_star_reviews.text:
Rude, bad attitude and extremely poor customer service.

We took a short trip to this little town to explore and enjoy what it has to offer, but unfortunately ended up having such a disappointing experience.

We went into the shop and my 14-year-old son was looking at a squeezy toy. The toy was inside a box with a small opening specifically allowing customers to pinch and try it. Obviously, the packaging was designed to allow customers to feel the toy before deciding whether to buy it.

My son was simply squeezing the toy through the opening and squeeze some other inside the cheap plastic bag. He was not making a mess, or tear of the packaging, screaming, running around, throwing things or disturbing anyone.

The older man then got angry and told my 14-year-old son, “Stop squeezing it if you’re not buying it, otherwise get out.”

We are not saying we were 100% right. If the shop does not want customers to squeeze the toys, he could have simply and politely said, “Please stop squeezing it if you’re not planning to buy it.” We would have understood and stopped immediately.

But there was absolutely no need to add “otherwise get out.” That was rude, unnecessary and completely inappropriate when speaking to a 14-year-old child.

And honestly, it’s not like we can’t afford to buy that cheap little toy. We were simply looking at it and deciding whether to purchase it. Being treated like that over a little squeezy toy was ridiculous.

If customers are not allowed to try the toys, then put up a clear sign saying “Please do not squeeze” instead of getting angry at customers for doing something the packaging itself appears to invite them to do.

What made the situation even more unacceptable was that he repeatedly told us to “get out”, even though we were not behaving aggressively, causing any disturbance, or doing anything inappropriate. We were simply looking at the products.

He was the one who turned such a tiny and insignificant matter into a ridiculous confrontation. There was absolutely no need to repeatedly tell customers to “get out” over something so minor.

We have lived in New Zealand for 10–20 years, and this is honestly the first time we have experienced this kind of treatment in a shop.

It made us wonder — was this racism?

We came to this little town simply to explore its beauty and enjoy the trip, and unfortunately this unpleasant experience has left a very negative impression of our visit.

Very disappointing. The way you speak to customers, especially children, matters. Good luck with your business

I understand that I called around 10 minutes before closing, and I appreciate that this may not have been the ideal time to contact customer service. However, I had attempted to call several times before this and was either hung up on or left waiting in the queue for more than 10 minutes, so I was unable to get through earlier.

When an agent finally answered, the experience was extremely disappointing. He sounded clearly unimpressed that I was calling and seemed to be rushing me through my enquiry. I acknowledge that I am currently behind on my account, but I have been making consistent payments to bring the balance up to date.

The agent advised me that I was still behind and provided the amount outstanding. I explained that I wanted to understand exactly what was required so that I could plan my payments and get the account up to date sooner rather than later. He simply repeated that changes could not be made until the account was up to date and that I would need to wait 24 hours for payments to appear.

I thanked him for the information, and he immediately responded with “thank you, bye.” There was no attempt to ask whether there was anything else he could assist me with, and his tone throughout the conversation was unpleasant and dismissive.

I understand that customer service staff deal with difficult calls and busy periods, but customers should still be treated with basic courtesy and professionalism. Being behind on an account does not mean a customer deserves to be spoken to dismissively, particularly when they are actively making payments and trying to resolve the situation.

I hope management takes this feedback seriously and uses it as a learning opportunity for the Customer Service Team, particularly in relation to improving the overall customer experience.

one_star_reviews.text: Kind ruined my life temporarily. I hate to be a downer but honestly taking stimulants and mood stabilisers was probably the worse thing to ever happen in my life, I understand that medication takes trail and error but this error took a lot of time to reverse. I have been tapering off of lamotrigine, likely the worst drug I’ve ever taken because of how long it takes to come off of. I have been tapering for 6-7 months and still going. I don’t like the fact that when I am at low like I was it costed even more money. I appreciate my psychiatrist’s care, but I wanted to share some feedback on my experience. Starting Concerta while I was still experiencing venlafaxine withdrawal, combined with the timing of lamotrigine, caused significant overstimulation, anxiety, and distress. Given my autism and dual diagnoses, greater sensitivity could have been anticipated, and a more cautious, individualized approach to stimulant initiation and mood stabilizer timing would have helped prevent the trauma I experienced. While I value the support I received, I think clearer guidance and spacing of medications would improve the patient experience for neurodivergent individuals with complex medication needs. I will likely follow up with my doctor eventually about dosage, but for now I’m keeping things stable. Please be aware, if you are autistic too, this combination can be overwhelming.

one_star_reviews.text:
Just coming back to clarify a few things after reading the manager’s response, because several claims made here simply do not match what actually happened.

Firstly, we were not in the venue for three hours. We were there for approximately 1 hour and 20 minutes at most, and some of our group left even earlier. So the claim that we were there for three hours, or spent “well over two hours” watching the dancers, is simply not true.

For a significant amount of the time we were there, there wasn’t even a dancer performing on the floor. From what we actually saw, we watched maybe two dancers perform during our entire visit. The suggestion that we spent hours sitting there watching dancers perform for free is a complete misrepresentation of our experience.

When we entered, the rule explained to us was clear: if we sat in the lounge/couch area near the dancers, we were expected to tip. If we sat at the tables, tipping was not required. Interestingly, the manager’s own response confirms that tipping was not mandatory at the tables.

For most of our visit, we were sitting towards the back. It was only during roughly the last 20–30 minutes that we moved chairs forward so we could actually see the show while still being able to talk amongst ourselves.

The manager also claims that dancers approached us and “invited” us to tip. That does not accurately describe the interaction we had. One dancer came over and had a perfectly normal conversation with us about how much a dance would cost. The conversation was about purchasing a dance, not asking us to tip. There was no issue with her whatsoever.

As for the claim that I only asked for $5 at the bar, that completely misses what I was trying to ask. I was asking about getting $5 notes and how many I could get, because I intended to get more money out for tipping. There was clearly a misunderstanding. Instead of simply asking me to clarify what I meant, the bartender became unnecessarily hostile and rude.

And that is exactly what the original review was about. The bartender was genuinely one of the rudest staff members I have encountered at a venue. We were incredibly disappointed by the way she spoke to and treated us. A simple misunderstanding that could have been resolved in seconds instead turned into an unnecessarily hostile interaction.

We also purchased approximately three or four drinks during the relatively short period we were there.

Nobody expected the dancers to work “pro bono”, and the sarcastic Latin lesson doesn’t change what happened. We followed the rules as they were explained to us, purchased drinks, and were actually attempting to organise money for tipping when the interaction at the bar occurred.

Instead of addressing a legitimate complaint about customer service, the manager has responded by disputing our timeline, misrepresenting interactions and publicly calling customers “pubescent boys”.

Your response honestly just reinforces our original review. The way management has chosen to speak to customers publicly shows exactly why we were so disappointed with how we were treated in person. Rather than handling criticism professionally, you’ve responded with insults, sarcasm and claims about our visit that simply don’t reflect what happened.

It shows an incredibly poor attitude towards customers, and after seeing the way management responds to criticism, the other 1-star reviews now make a lot more sense. It all adds up.

If anything, your response has done a better job of proving the point of our original review than we ever could.

I then called two other stores, both of whom told me that because the item was faulty and I hadn’t damaged it, I could return it. These phone calls also highlighted how unprofessional the Porirua team had been.

I had some good customer service here from the reception, However an ugly experience with one of the NP's here today. Her name is Akanksha Sethi. I came in for a check up with my Mum, who is experiencing her own health issues one being memory loss. Look I get these guys probably deal with alot of defensive family members for their loved ones, But from the moment we met I was Polite, diplomatic, and thought I was raising fair concerns and questions about my mums health and how there can be a good plan of Acton to help her get better . Akanksha was really dismissive towards our input, Rude, had passive aggression, cutting me off for her own observations rather than just hearing out what I needed to mention I felt was important, I told her she was not being professional, and she continued to argue over that statement, make threats to cancel what was already urgently needed for my mum, which was an iron Transfusion along with other serious symptoms I wanted checked on my Mum. All I was asking for was the process and a clear line of communication for next steps but got eye rolls from her instead. She had no patience for this, made the threats and just sugguested we go with another doctor before storming out to reception. We waited patiently until she finished her tantrum, she then came back realising what she had done. So she re booked the iron transfusion and cancelled everything else id say is urgent and said we have to go over everything again with another doctor. This annoyed me because I see it as refusing health care, unprofessional and definitely would not want someone like this watching over a loved one in need of help. She seemed like the type who wanted to do bare minimum, doesn't like any questions or request's basically hated being told to do anything extra than what she probably thinks is easiest.
She seemed nice at first but it just took a massive turn with her attitude when asking for help and next steps to follow, all she had to do was act in a professional manner and give advice and even keep the other booking she well knew were urgently needed from our side. The eye rolls, the threats the tantrum was all very crap care service for someone in her position, and how do you expect your patients to react to this sort of behaviour.

I spoke to another lady at the counter who demonstrated better understanding and at least a bit of care towards what I was asking for who said I can try again with another doctor from the same clinic.  I have lived and grown up In Otahuhu and it is disappointing to see this is our level of health care today. Maybe I caught her at a bad day or just got unlucky getting her as maybe shes always like this, either way she gives this clinic a bad name and Im glad we wont be dealing with her again. I hope this reaches higher level where someone can follow up on this with her.

I had a very disappointing experience at Horizontal Radiology Ōtara.

I understand that the correct referral form is required, but the situation could have been avoided if someone had been available at reception when we arrived. We were told to wait because other people were there, and this delay ultimately affected our appointment.

I hope the centre can improve its reception service and communication so other patients do not experience the same issue.

My wife and I had a very negative and disappointing experience with Sorena Study Limited. We paid NZ$2,800 for immigration services in 2021, but after nearly five years of litigation, we were finally forced to go to the Disputes Tribunal of New Zealand to get our money back.

one_star_reviews.text:
We went to New World Winton yesterday to do our grocery shopping and unfortunately we were quite disappointed with one of the items my mum purchased.

She bought a large yoghurt for around $3 ish, not realising that it had been reduced. She only noticed today, when she was about to eat it, that the best before date was actually today. She then checked her receipt and realised that it had been marked down.

We understand that products close to their best-before date can be reduced but selling a large yoghurt at that price when it expires the very next day feels disappointing, especially when the reduced price wasn’t something she noticed at the time of purchase. We feel products with such a short date should be clearly marked so customers can make an informed decision.

My mum has lived in New Zealand for 18 years and has also noticed on several occasions that some items displayed in the aisles as “SALE” don’t always seem to be genuinely reduced compared with their usual price. This can be quite confusing and from a customer’s perspective, feels misleading.

We normally shop at New World and would simply like to see clearer and more transparent pricing, especially when it comes to sale and reduced items. Hopefully this can be looked into.

I have regularly used Just Cuts in the past.  Being able to use their app to see the wait time and get in the queue has been one of the good features.  However, it failed miserably today.  I was given a wait time of 70 mins.  I managed (struggled patiently) to fill that time around the shops and with a coffee etc whilst watching the time counting down on the app.  It got to 3 minutes to go, so I went into Just Cuts and waited.  My app then said that I am next.  Woo hoo I thought.  Then the assistant called out someone else's name.  I showed her my phone that said I was next and she said 'there are 4 people in front of you'.  I asked 'why does the app say that I am next?'  She replied 'I don't know'.
Did all these other people that came in, in the last 70 minutes push in front of me?  Is the app actually connected to what is going on in the store? What is the point of the app if it is not connected to reality.  If you want to really annoy someone.  Give them a wait time.  Give them an expected appointment time.  And then when they get there, tell them that they have to wair for 4 other people who most likely came in after them and haven't used the system.  Really disappointed.

one_star_reviews.text:
I’m sharing this review based on my own experience and the invoices/service records I have.

Around 6 months ago, we took our car to Midas Manukau because we were having a spark plug issue. We were advised to replace all the spark plugs and ignition coils, and we were told that the replacement came with a 2-year warranty. We trusted their advice and paid around $3,000 for the work.

Unfortunately, the same problem came back after about a month. After that, it happened again and again — more than five times in total. Each time, we contacted them, and they arranged to collect the car and carry out further servicing.

To be fair, because they had provided a 2-year warranty, they did not charge us anything for these repeated repairs during the warranty period. They also paid for our WOF. However, despite all these repairs, the underlying problem was never properly resolved.

What concerns us even more is that the car was technically not fit to be driven safely, despite having a current WOF. We later took the car to a Honda service centre, where we were told that the engine had a major problem and would need to be replaced. We were shocked.

When we later had the car inspected before selling it, we were also surprised to learn that the spark plugs and coils that had been installed were apparently low-cost parts, despite us paying around $3,000 for the work at Midas.

Eventually, we had no choice but to sell the car for only $800.

I want to acknowledge that Midas did honour the warranty in the sense that they did not charge us for the repeated repair attempts, and they also covered the WOF. However, after experiencing the same issue more than five times and eventually being told by Honda that the engine needed to be replaced, we are extremely disappointed with the overall outcome.

My recommendation to other customers: if you are considering using this service centre, make sure you get a detailed quotation, check exactly which parts are being installed, ask about the brand and quality of the parts, and consider getting a second opinion from another reputable service centre before agreeing to major repairs.

I have kept the invoices and other documentation relating to this experience and can provide them as evidence of what I have described.

This is my personal experience and my honest review. I hope other customers are careful and ask questions before spending a significant amount of money on repairs.

Thank you.

What we were sold: a zoned ducted system giving per-room temperature control and automatic changeover between heating and cooling.

What we have: a system that delivers neither. For the past year we have logged the app settings against independent thermometer readings in each room. Technicians have attended numerous times, including a visit on 30/07/2026 where sensor readings had to be corrected and the underlying problem is still there.

Despite several emails from our side we have had no substantive response to any of them.

We should not have had to chase any of this. A customer buying a complete zoned system is entitled to a system that does what it was sold to do and to be told which parts of it the manufacturer will not stand behind. That obligation sits with the installer, not with us.

Panasonic New Zealand have referred the matter to an independent service representative for a written technical assessment.

On our experience, I would not deal with Comfy Kiwi Homes or with its director Sean Childs and I would advise anyone considering a ducted install to go elsewhere.

one_star_reviews.text:
Whangārei Hospital

Honestly, our experience at Whangārei Hospital was extremely disappointing. My baby mama wasn’t feeling well and had to wait hours just to be seen by a doctor. She was made to have multiple blood tests to check if anything was wrong, but there was very little explanation about what was actually happening.

She was moved between different rooms multiple times, with no obvious change in what was being done, which only seemed to make the wait even longer. When the doctor finally came in, there was barely any explanation or communication about what was happening. Instead, more blood was taken, and we were left wondering what the reason was.

What made it even worse was seeing doctors standing in the hallway using their devices while patients were waiting right in front of them. There were babies, children and other patients needing attention. We also saw an older man asking for help and appearing to be brushed off.

At one point, staff even walked past my baby mama while the curtain was open, which felt incredibly disrespectful and careless.

⭐️ Extremely disappointing and unprofessional experience
I booked an appointment at Rodney Wayne Newmarket this morning for a 10:00am hair colour appointment with a trainee. When I booked the appointment, I was told I could come at 10:00am, but I was never informed that payment had to be made in cash.

I travelled approximately 40 minutes to get to the salon, only to be told upon arrival by the manager/trainer that the service would only be provided if I paid in cash. As I had not been informed of this requirement, I did not have my credit cards with me. Instead of acknowledging that this was a communication failure on their end, the trainer/manager was extremely rude and dismissive about the situation.

After I pointed out that I had not been told about the cash-only requirement, she eventually agreed to accept payment by bank transfer. However, the situation then became even more frustrating. She told me that she was short on time and would therefore only do a half-head colour/the crown rather than the service I had originally booked.

At that point, having already travelled 40 minutes and spent a significant amount of time dealing with an issue that was not my fault, I reluctantly agreed to go ahead with the half-head service.

Then, incredibly, she pointed to the trainee, who was apparently upset and crying, and said that she could no longer provide the service. I was left completely stunned.

Whatever internal issues, miscommunication or training-related problems were happening between the staff should never have been made the client's problem. If a trainee was upset, that should have been dealt with privately and professionally by the manager. Instead, I was left standing there after travelling 40 minutes for an appointment that the salon had confirmed.

I have never experienced such a lack of professionalism from a salon. The manager/trainer should have taken responsibility for the communication failure, handled the situation calmly, and made a genuine effort to provide the service I had booked — particularly after I had already made the way to the salon.

Very disappointing customer service and extremely poor management. I would not recommend booking an appointment here, especially if you are expecting basic communication, professionalism and respect for your time.

I would have preferred to contact Templeton Medical Centre directly by email, but the clinic does not appear to operate an email system, so I’m raising this concern here.

I’m extremely disappointed by the advice given to my elderly grandmother, who is a long-standing patient of the clinic. She sustained a wound last night which continued bleeding throughout the night. Given that she is on blood-thinning medication following multiple strokes, I am extremely concerned about the potential risks and feel this clearly needed to be attended to.

When the clinic could not see her, she was told to go to Rolleston After Hours immediately. However, Rolleston After Hours does not open until 5pm “…approximately seven hours after she called. This left her confused about where she was supposed to go and what she should do in the meantime a she didn’t even know where rolleston after hours is or where to find the it where it is. I had to call the clinic myself to clarify the advice, but received no acknowledgement that the information given to her had been unclear or inappropriate.

I understand that medical centres are under significant pressure, particularly during winter, and that the clinic may not have had appointments available. However, directing a fragile elderly patient to a service that was not open, without providing clear alternative advice, was inappropriate and concerning.

The clinic should consider providing patients with clear information about local alternative medical services and their opening hours when appointments are unavailable. This could simply be printed and kept next to the phone at reception so it’s easy to find when patients call. Patients need appropriate guidance, particularly when they may be confused or unable to navigate unfamiliar situations independently.

If your child has genuine ambition to become a real footballer, do not waste a single season sending them to Rovers.

The club's ineptness is staggering. There is zero technical training, no stamina conditioning, and absolute ignorance regarding mental preparation. The entire program is run by an outdated coach who is completely checked out—indifferent to the kids' growth and utterly uninterested in actual coaching. It feels less like a developmental football program and more like a high-priced babysitting service.

What makes it truly infuriating is the demand on the parents. Dragging your kids to training twice a week and showing up every single weekend—burning precious time, effort, and petrol money—only to sit there and witness a complete waste of time. You watch dedicated kids stuck in an unmotivated environment led by a club that only cares about taking your fees.

The psychological toll on ambitious players is unacceptable. Kids arrive at the start of the year with high standards and a drive to win, only to spend the season systematically taught to accept mediocrity and be comfortable as losers.

If you care about your child’s athletic future—and value your own time and money—avoid this club.

one_star_reviews.text:
I don’t recommend this insurance company based on my recent experience.

I applied for a special events increase of up to an additional $100,000 to my existing life insurance policy. What I expected to be a relatively straightforward increase has turned into a lengthy process requiring multiple pieces of documentation, including specific evidence from my mortgage lender and my solicitor.

I had already provided documentation showing that I have a mortgage with a lender, including the Land Transfer/Record of Title showing the registered mortgage (which my solicitor said should be sufficient), plus the facility agreement from the lender. Despite this, this still didn't seem to be enough. I was asked to obtain further information on the lender’s letterhead, including the mortgage drawdown date, details of those liable for the mortgage, the solicitor’s payment schedule, and verification that the mortgage was unconditional.

For an additional $100,000 of cover which wouldn’t even cover any where near my mortgage anyway, I simply didn’t feel the amount of extra cover was worth the time and hassle involved in obtaining all of this documentation. I've now asked for the increase application to be withdrawn.

I am now working with an insurance broker to look at obtaining a new policy elsewhere for an amount that will actually provide meaningful cover for my mortgage.

I appreciate that insurers have underwriting and verification requirements, but in my experience, the process became unnecessarily difficult and lengthy for the relatively small increase in cover I was seeking.
